metaDescription: Center City Philadelphia general contractor. Condo renovations, historic restoration, and high-end kitchen & bath remodels in Rittenhouse & Society Hill.
heroHeading: Center City Philadelphia's Trusted General Contractor
heroSubheading: Premium condo renovations, historic brownstone restoration, and high-end remodeling from Rittenhouse Square to Old City.
introduction:
Center City Philadelphia is one of the most architecturally diverse and demanding markets for a general contractor. From the stately 19th-century brownstones along Pine and Spruce Streets to the converted warehouse lofts of Old City and the glass-and-steel high-rises that define the Rittenhouse skyline, every project here comes with its own set of challenges — and we know them all.

We've spent years working inside the tight freight elevators of condo towers on Walnut Street, navigating HOA approval processes for buildings like The Dorchester, The Philadelphian, and Hopkinson House, and pulling permits through L&I for historically designated properties in Society Hill. We understand that a kitchen remodel on the 30th floor of a Rittenhouse high-rise requires a completely different logistics plan than a gut renovation of a three-story brownstone in Washington Square West.

Center City's housing stock ranges from 1700s-era Federal-style rowhomes in Society Hill to 1960s concrete-frame towers to brand-new luxury condos. Many of these older buildings come with galvanized steel plumbing, outdated 100-amp electrical panels, plaster-and-lath walls, and original hardwood floors worth preserving. We know when to restore and when to replace, and we have relationships with specialty subcontractors who handle things like plaster crown molding replication, marble hearth restoration, and period-appropriate millwork.

Parking and access are real cost factors in Center City. Street permits, loading zones, material staging in narrow alleys, and coordinating deliveries before rush hour are all part of our daily operations here. We build these logistics into our bids upfront so there are no surprises. If your building requires COIs, move-in/move-out scheduling, or construction hour restrictions, we've handled it before — probably in your building.

faqs.question: Do I need special permits for renovating a historic property in Society Hill?
faqs.answer: Yes. Properties within the Society Hill Historic District or individually designated on the Philadelphia Register of Historic Places require review by the Philadelphia Historical Commission before any exterior alterations — and sometimes interior structural changes. We handle the application process and coordinate with the Commission to ensure your project stays on schedule and in compliance.

faqs.question: How do you handle renovations in high-rise condo buildings with strict building rules?
faqs.answer: We're experienced with HOA and building management requirements across Center City. We carry the insurance minimums most buildings require (typically $2M general liability), coordinate material deliveries around freight elevator schedules, observe quiet hours and construction windows, and manage dust and debris containment to protect common areas. We also handle all COI requests and pre-construction walkthroughs with building management.

faqs.question: Why are Center City renovation costs higher than other parts of Philly?
faqs.answer: Several factors drive higher costs: limited street parking means paying for loading zone permits and off-peak deliveries, freight elevator scheduling affects labor productivity in high-rises, older buildings often reveal hidden issues behind walls (knob-and-tube wiring, lead paint, deteriorated plumbing), and the premium finishes Center City homeowners expect — think Calacatta marble, custom cabinetry, and designer fixtures — carry higher material costs.

faqs.question: Can you work with my architect or interior designer on a Center City project?
faqs.answer: Absolutely — and we often do. Many of our Center City projects involve collaboration with design professionals. We're comfortable working from full architectural drawings or partnering early in the design process to provide constructability input and realistic budgeting before plans are finalized.

faqs.question: How long does a typical condo renovation take in Center City?
faqs.answer: A full condo gut renovation (kitchen, bathrooms, flooring, paint, lighting) typically runs 8–14 weeks depending on unit size and scope. Kitchen-only remodels average 5–7 weeks. We always factor in building-specific constraints like elevator access and construction hour limits when setting timelines.

testimonial.name: David M.
testimonial.text: We hired JD Home to completely renovate our 2-bedroom condo in Rittenhouse Square. They navigated the building's strict renovation rules seamlessly, kept the hallways spotless, and delivered a stunning kitchen with custom walnut cabinetry and a marble waterfall island. The project manager was on-site daily and communicated with our building's management better than we could have. Final result was worth every penny.

name: Fishtown & Northern Liberties
metaTitle: General Contractor in Fishtown & Northern Liberties | JD Home Construction
metaDescription: Fishtown & Northern Liberties general contractor specializing in gut renovations, open-concept conversions, and rowhouse remodels. Expert local knowledge since day one.
heroSubheading: Gut renovations, open-concept conversions, and full rowhouse remodels in Philly's fastest-evolving neighborhoods.
introduction:
Fishtown and Northern Liberties have transformed dramatically over the past two decades, and we've been renovating homes here through every phase of that evolution. What were once affordable rowhomes built for factory workers along the Delaware River waterfront are now some of the most sought-after properties in Philadelphia — and they come with renovation challenges that only a contractor who truly knows these blocks can anticipate.

The typical Fishtown rowhome was built between 1880 and 1930, originally as a two-story or three-story brick row with a galley kitchen, single bathroom, and narrow floor plan — usually 14 to 16 feet wide. Behind the walls, you'll commonly find knob-and-tube wiring, clay sewer laterals that have shifted or cracked, galvanized water supply lines, and original plaster over wood lath. We've opened up hundreds of these walls and know exactly what to expect and how to bring them up to modern code without losing the character that drew homeowners here in the first place.

Open-concept conversions are the most requested project type in Fishtown. Homeowners want to remove the wall between the living room and kitchen, creating a single flowing space from the front door to the back of the house. This almost always involves structural steel — a properly engineered beam to replace the load-bearing wall — and we work with licensed structural engineers to size every beam correctly for the span and load. We don't guess on structure.

Northern Liberties has its own personality: more loft-style condos in converted industrial buildings along 2nd and 3rd Streets, mixed with newer townhome construction. We handle both — from restoring exposed brick and timber in a converted warehouse unit to finishing out a brand-new construction townhome that the builder left with basic-grade finishes. The mix of old and new here keeps every project interesting.

faqs.question: How much does a full gut renovation cost for a Fishtown rowhouse?
faqs.answer: A full gut renovation of a typical 1,200–1,600 sq ft Fishtown rowhouse — including new electrical, plumbing, HVAC, kitchen, bathrooms, flooring, and finishes — generally ranges from $150,000 to $250,000 depending on finishes and structural changes. Open-concept conversions requiring structural steel add $8,000–$15,000 to the scope. We provide detailed line-item estimates after an in-home assessment.

faqs.question: Is knob-and-tube wiring dangerous? Do I need to replace it?
faqs.answer: Knob-and-tube wiring isn't inherently dangerous if undisturbed, but it's not designed for modern electrical loads, can't be covered with insulation, and most insurance companies won't write a policy on a home with active K&T. In any significant renovation, we recommend full replacement with modern Romex wiring and an upgraded 200-amp panel. It's usually required by code once walls are opened.

faqs.question: Can you help with a rear addition on a Fishtown rowhouse?
faqs.answer: Yes — rear additions (sometimes called bump-outs) are one of our specialties. Fishtown's narrow lots mean the only direction to expand is usually toward the back. We handle everything from zoning review and permit applications through L&I to structural engineering, foundation work, and finish carpentry. Depending on depth, you may be able to add 100–200 square feet to your first floor.

faqs.question: Do I need a permit for interior renovations in Philadelphia?
faqs.answer: Most interior renovations that involve structural changes, electrical work, plumbing modifications, or HVAC changes require permits through Philadelphia's Department of Licenses & Inspections (L&I). Cosmetic work like painting, flooring, and cabinet replacement typically doesn't. We handle all permit applications and schedule required inspections as part of our standard process.

testimonial.name: Sarah & Tom K.

They found knob-and-tube behind every wall, a cracked sewer line, and a sagging second floor — and handled all of it without missing a beat. The open-concept first floor with the steel beam is exactly what we envisioned. They were honest about costs from day one and the final number came in right where they said it would.

name: South Philadelphia
metaTitle: General Contractor in South Philadelphia | JD Home Construction
metaDescription: South Philadelphia general contractor specializing in rowhouse renovations, kitchen expansions, concrete repair, and bathroom modernization. Passyunk to Point Breeze.
heroSubheading: Rowhouse renovations, kitchen expansions, concrete stoop repair, and bathroom remodels across South Philly's iconic neighborhoods.
introduction:
South Philadelphia is the heart of classic Philly rowhouse living, and renovating these homes requires a contractor who respects their bones while knowing how to modernize them for today's families. From the brick-front rows along Passyunk Avenue to the ornate Victorian facades of Queen Village and the tightly packed streets of Bella Vista near the Italian Market, South Philly's housing stock is almost entirely pre-1930 — and much of it predates 1910.

These homes were built solid: triple-wythe brick walls, slate or tin roofs, plaster over wood lath, and cast iron waste stacks that have been running for over a century. But a century of use takes its toll. The most common issues we encounter in South Philly are failing cast iron plumbing stacks that need replacement with PVC, settlement cracks in party walls from decades of soil movement, galvanized water supply lines that restrict flow to a trickle, and kitchens so small that the refrigerator blocks a doorway. We've solved every one of these problems hundreds of times.

Kitchen reconfiguration is the number-one request in South Philadelphia. The original galley kitchens in these rowhouses were designed for an era of iceboxes and coal stoves — they're simply too small for modern living. We specialize in reconfiguring first-floor layouts to create functional, beautiful kitchens without sacrificing structural integrity. This often involves relocating plumbing, adjusting load paths, and creatively using every inch of a 14-foot-wide footprint.

Outside, South Philly's concrete stoops, sidewalks, and basement hatchways take a beating from freeze-thaw cycles. We handle concrete replacement, stoop rebuilds, and facade pointing — keeping your home's curb appeal sharp and your liability exposure low. Point Breeze and Grays Ferry are seeing a wave of renovation investment right now, and we're proud to be part of the revitalization while keeping the neighborhood's character intact.

faqs.question: My South Philly rowhouse kitchen is tiny — can you actually make it bigger?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it's our most common project in South Philly. We typically reconfigure the first-floor layout by removing or relocating non-load-bearing walls, sometimes borrowing space from an adjacent dining room or unused pantry closet. In some cases, a small rear bump-out of 4–6 feet makes a dramatic difference. We work within your budget and the realities of a narrow rowhouse footprint to maximize every square foot.

faqs.question: Do I need to replace the cast iron plumbing in my rowhouse?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily all of it, but if your cast iron waste stack is showing signs of failure — slow drains across multiple fixtures, sewage odors, visible corrosion or holes, or wet spots on basement walls — it's time. Most South Philly rowhouses have a single main stack that runs from basement to roof. Replacing it with PVC is a 2–3 day job for our plumbing crew and prevents a catastrophic failure that could cause significant water damage.

faqs.question: How much does concrete stoop replacement cost in South Philly?
faqs.answer: A standard South Philly stoop replacement — demo of the existing stoop, new formed and poured concrete steps with a landing, and railing — typically runs $4,500–$8,000 depending on size and complexity. If the sidewalk and curb also need work, we can usually bundle that at a better rate. We obtain the required L&I permits and ensure compliance with ADA slope requirements where applicable.

faqs.question: Can you match the original brick and mortar when repointing my facade?
faqs.answer: Yes — and this is critical. Using modern Portland cement mortar on historic soft brick will actually accelerate deterioration because the hard mortar traps moisture and causes the softer brick to spall. We use lime-based mortar that matches the original composition and color, and we source matching brick from salvage yards when replacements are needed. Proper pointing extends the life of your facade by decades.

faqs.question: Is Point Breeze a good area to invest in a renovation?
faqs.answer: Point Breeze has seen strong appreciation over the past decade and continues to attract buyers and investors. Renovated rowhomes in Point Breeze are selling well above the area median. We've completed numerous renovations in Point Breeze and Newbold and can advise on which improvements offer the best return on investment for the current market.

testimonial.name: Angela R.
testimonial.text: Our 1912 rowhouse in Passyunk Square had the original everything — including a kitchen that hadn't been touched since the 1970s. JD Home reconfigured our entire first floor, opened up the kitchen into the dining area, replaced the ancient plumbing stack, and gave us a bathroom that actually fits two people. They knew exactly what to expect behind the walls and never once seemed surprised by what they found. Real pros who know South Philly homes inside and out.

name: Manayunk & Roxborough
metaTitle: General Contractor in Manayunk & Roxborough | JD Home Construction
metaDescription: Manayunk & Roxborough general contractor. Decks, retaining walls, basement waterproofing, and full remodels for hillside homes. Licensed & insured in Philadelphia.
heroSubheading: Decks, retaining walls, basement waterproofing, and full renovations for the unique hillside homes of Northwest Philadelphia.
introduction:
Manayunk and Roxborough present some of the most unique construction challenges in all of Philadelphia. Built into the steep hills above the Schuylkill River and Wissahickon Creek, these neighborhoods have dramatic grade changes that affect everything from foundation integrity to water drainage to how we stage materials on a job site. A contractor who doesn't understand hillside construction has no business working here — and we've been building on these slopes for years.

The housing stock in Manayunk and Roxborough is genuinely varied. Along Main Street and the side streets climbing up from the canal towpath, you'll find narrow Victorian-era twins and rows originally built for mill workers in the late 1800s. Up in Roxborough proper, the homes transition to larger mid-century singles and twins from the 1940s through 1960s, many with stone facades, detached garages, and actual yards. East Falls adds another layer with its mix of stately singles and apartment conversions near Kelly Drive.

Water is the number-one enemy in this area. The steep terrain channels rainwater downhill with force, and homes on the low side of the street are especially vulnerable. We see chronic basement water intrusion, failed French drains, deteriorated retaining walls, and foundation erosion regularly. Our approach starts with understanding the water's path — we don't just patch symptoms, we solve the drainage problem at its source with proper grading, French drain systems, sump pump installations, and exterior waterproofing membranes.

Decks and outdoor living spaces are hugely popular here because many of these homes have rear yards that overlook the Wissahickon Valley or the Manayunk canal. We build decks, multi-level outdoor spaces, and retaining wall systems that work with the terrain rather than fighting it. Pressure-treated lumber, composite decking, and properly engineered footings on grade are standard for our hillside builds.

faqs.question: Why does my Manayunk basement flood every time it rains?
faqs.answer: Manayunk's steep terrain channels large volumes of rainwater downhill, and homes on the lower side of sloped streets take the brunt of it. Common culprits include clogged or nonexistent French drains, negative grading around the foundation, failed exterior waterproofing membranes, and undersized or broken sump pumps. We start with a thorough assessment of water entry points and drainage paths, then design a solution that may include exterior grading corrections, a perimeter French drain system, interior drainage channels, and a reliable sump pump with battery backup.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to build a deck in Manayunk or Roxborough?
faqs.answer: Deck costs in this area vary significantly because of the hillside factor. A simple ground-level deck on a flat lot might run $8,000–$15,000, but a multi-level deck built on a steep grade with engineered footings, stairs, and railings can range from $20,000–$45,000+. Composite materials like Trex or TimberTech add to the material cost but dramatically reduce long-term maintenance. We provide detailed estimates after a site visit to assess grade and access.

faqs.question: My retaining wall is leaning — is that an emergency?
faqs.answer: A leaning retaining wall is a serious structural concern, especially on Manayunk's steep lots where a failure can affect your foundation or your neighbor's property. If the lean is noticeable or has worsened recently, we recommend a prompt evaluation. We assess the wall's construction, drainage condition, and soil pressure to determine whether it can be repaired or needs full replacement with a properly engineered and permitted wall system.

faqs.question: Do I need a permit for a deck in Philadelphia?
faqs.answer: Yes — any deck that's attached to the house or elevated more than 30 inches above grade requires a building permit from L&I. Decks over a certain size may also trigger a zoning review. We handle the full permit process, including structural drawings and zoning applications, so the project is fully legal and inspected.

faqs.question: Can you replace the old aluminum siding on my Roxborough twin?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Many 1950s and 1960s twins in Roxborough still have original aluminum siding that's dented, faded, and no longer weather-tight. We install fiber cement (James Hardie), vinyl, and engineered wood siding with proper housewrap and flashing. This is also the ideal time to add insulation and address any sheathing damage underneath.

testimonial.name: Mike & Jen P.
testimonial.text: Our Roxborough twin had a basement that flooded every spring and a backyard we couldn't use because of the slope. JD Home installed a full French drain system with a sump pump, regraded the side yard, and then built us a beautiful two-level composite deck overlooking the Wissahickon. The basement has been bone dry through two heavy rainstorms since, and the deck has become our favorite room in the house. These guys understand hillside homes.

name: Northeast Philadelphia
metaTitle: General Contractor in Northeast Philadelphia | JD Home Construction
metaDescription: Northeast Philadelphia general contractor for whole-home renovations, kitchen updates, bathroom remodels, roofing, siding, and home additions. Serving Bustleton to Somerton.
heroSubheading: Whole-home renovations, kitchen modernization, home additions, and exterior upgrades for the Northeast's single-family homes.
introduction:
Northeast Philadelphia is a world apart from Center City — and it requires a different kind of contractor. Out here, you're working on single-family homes with real yards, driveways, and often detached garages. The housing stock is predominantly post-war: ranch homes, split-levels, Cape Cods, and colonials built during the suburban boom of the 1950s through 1970s. These homes were solid when they were built, but after 50 to 70 years, they need serious updating to meet today's standards of comfort, efficiency, and style.

The most common situation we see in the Northeast is a home that's been well-maintained on the surface but never truly modernized. The kitchen still has its original layout with outdated oak cabinets and laminate countertops. The bathrooms have pink or green tile from the Eisenhower era. The windows are original single-pane aluminum sliders. The roof has been patched but needs full replacement. The finished basement has wood paneling and drop ceilings from 1975. Sound familiar? We renovate dozens of these homes every year.

Northeast Philly homeowners tend to be practical, value-conscious, and planning to stay in their homes long-term — which means they want renovations that improve daily living, not just resale value. We approach every project with that mindset: recommending durable materials that perform for decades, energy-efficient windows and insulation that lower utility bills, and layouts that work for how families actually live.

Home additions are also a strong segment in the Northeast because the larger lots allow for it. Whether it's a family room addition off the back, a second-story addition on a ranch, or an in-law suite over the garage, the space and zoning here generally support expansion in ways that tighter neighborhoods can't. We handle the full scope from architectural plans and permits through foundation, framing, and finish work.

faqs.question: Is it worth doing a full renovation on a 1960s ranch home in the Northeast?
faqs.answer: In most cases, absolutely. Northeast Philly ranches have solid bones — concrete block or poured foundations, good-sized lots, and simple roof lines that are inexpensive to maintain. A full renovation (kitchen, baths, flooring, paint, updated electrical and plumbing) typically costs significantly less than buying a comparable new-construction home, and you end up with a property that's customized to your needs. We see strong ROI on these projects, especially when energy efficiency upgrades are included.

faqs.question: Can you add a second story to my ranch home?
faqs.answer: Yes, second-story additions on ranch homes are one of our specialties. The process involves engineering the existing foundation and first-floor structure to verify they can support the additional load, then framing the second story, adding stairs, and tying into existing HVAC, plumbing, and electrical systems. A typical second-story addition in the Northeast adds 600–1,000 square feet and runs $150,000–$250,000+ depending on scope and finishes.

faqs.question: How do I know if my roof needs replacement or just repair?
faqs.answer: If your roof is original to a 1960s or 1970s home, it's likely past its useful life even if it's been patched over the years. Signs that replacement is needed include curling or missing shingles, granules in your gutters, daylight visible from the attic, multiple layers of roofing (common in the Northeast — we regularly tear off 2–3 layers), and any active leaks. We provide free roof assessments and honest recommendations.

faqs.question: Do you handle aging-in-place modifications?
faqs.answer: Yes — this is a growing need in Northeast Philadelphia where many homeowners are long-term residents who want to stay in their homes. We install walk-in showers with grab bars, widen doorways for wheelchair access, add first-floor bedroom and bath conversions, install stairlifts, and improve lighting and flooring for safety. Every modification is customized to the homeowner's specific mobility needs.

faqs.question: What's the permit process like for a home addition in Northeast Philadelphia?
faqs.answer: Home additions require permits through Philadelphia L&I, including zoning approval (to confirm setback and lot coverage compliance), a building permit with engineered structural plans, and trade permits for electrical, plumbing, and HVAC. The process typically takes 4–8 weeks for approvals. We manage the entire permit process, attend any required hearings, and coordinate all inspections through completion.

name: Bucks County & Surrounding Suburbs
metaTitle: General Contractor in Bucks County | JD Home Construction
metaDescription: Bucks County general contractor for home additions, kitchen & bath remodels, basement finishing, deck building, and new construction. Bensalem to Doylestown.
heroSubheading: Home additions, kitchen and bath remodels, outdoor living, and new construction across Bucks County's diverse communities.
introduction:
Bucks County is where Philadelphia's urban density gives way to suburban space — and with that space comes a completely different set of construction opportunities and challenges. From the densely packed split-levels of lower Bucks communities like Bensalem and Levittown to the custom estates and historic stone farmhouses of central Bucks in Doylestown and Newtown, we've worked across the full spectrum of what this county has to offer.

The original Levittown homes — built by William Levitt starting in 1952 — are an iconic part of lower Bucks County's housing stock. These Jubilees, Ranchers, Country Clubbers, and Cape Cods were revolutionary in their time, but at 70+ years old, they need comprehensive updating. We've renovated hundreds of Levitt homes and know their construction inside and out: the slab-on-grade foundations, the original steel casement windows, the radiant floor heating systems (copper tubing in the slab) that are often still partially functional. Each model has its own quirks, and we plan around them.

Moving north into communities like Warminster, Southampton, and Langhorne, the homes transition to 1970s–1990s colonials and contemporaries on larger lots. These homes have more conventional construction but still face age-related issues: aging roofs, outdated kitchens and baths, deck structures that have reached end-of-life, and basements that were never properly finished.

A key difference when working in Bucks County versus Philadelphia is the permit process. Instead of dealing with L&I, each township has its own building department with its own requirements, timelines, and inspection schedules. We're registered contractors in Bensalem, Bristol, Middletown, Northampton, Warminster, and multiple other Bucks County townships, and we know each department's process. This saves our clients weeks of delays that contractors unfamiliar with suburban permitting often encounter.

Home additions are our bread and butter in Bucks County. The larger lots and more flexible zoning allow for substantial expansions — master suite additions, family room wings, sunrooms, and even full second stories on ranch homes. We also handle significant outdoor living projects: multi-season rooms, composite decks, paver patios, and outdoor kitchens that take full advantage of the yard space city homeowners can only dream about.

faqs.question: Can you renovate my Levittown home without disturbing the radiant floor heating?
faqs.answer: Yes — and this is a critical consideration that many contractors overlook. Many original Levittown homes have copper radiant heating tubing embedded in the concrete slab floor. Before any work that involves cutting or drilling into the slab (such as adding a bathroom or relocating plumbing), we use thermal imaging to map the tubing runs. If the system is still functional, we work around it. If it's been abandoned, we plan accordingly for alternative heating. We've worked on all six Levitt models and understand their slab layouts.

faqs.question: How does the permit process differ in Bucks County compared to Philadelphia?
faqs.answer: In Philadelphia, all permits go through L&I (Licenses & Inspections), a single city department. In Bucks County, each township operates its own building department — Bensalem, Middletown, Northampton, Warminster, etc. — each with different application forms, fee schedules, review timelines, and inspection processes. Some townships require plan review by a third-party engineer. We're registered and experienced in all major Bucks County townships, which means we know exactly what each department expects and can keep your project moving without delays.

faqs.question: How much does a home addition cost in Bucks County?
faqs.answer: Home addition costs vary widely based on size, complexity, and finishes. A basic family room addition (200–300 sq ft) typically starts around $60,000–$90,000. A full master suite addition with bathroom runs $100,000–$175,000. A second-story addition on a ranch can range from $150,000–$300,000. These figures include foundation, framing, roofing, insulation, HVAC extension, electrical, plumbing (if applicable), and interior finishes. We provide detailed estimates after an in-home consultation.

faqs.question: Do you build new homes in Bucks County?
faqs.answer: Yes — we handle ground-up residential construction in Bucks County. Whether you've purchased a lot and need a custom home built or you're demolishing an existing structure to build new, we manage the entire process from site work and foundation through framing, mechanicals, and finish work. We work with your architect or can recommend design professionals we've partnered with successfully on past projects.

faqs.question: Can you finish my basement with an egress window for a legal bedroom?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Adding an egress window is one of the most valuable improvements you can make to a basement, both for safety and for creating a code-compliant bedroom or living space. We handle the window well excavation, foundation cutting, window installation, and all associated waterproofing. Combined with a full basement finish (framing, drywall, flooring, lighting, HVAC), you can add 500–1,000+ square feet of usable living space to your home.

testimonial.name: Chris & Lisa T.
testimonial.text: We needed more space for our growing family but loved our Warminster neighborhood and didn't want to move. Our neighbors keep asking for their card.
